articles.headline: La empresa del bus donde aparecieron las pastillas de éxtasis niega los hechos y el colegio prescinde de ella
articles.subtitle: El gerente asegura que el vehículo «foi limpado e revisado» y duda de que las pastillas estuvieran dentro. El centro, cliente suyo desde hace más de veinte años, ya le ha comunicado que deja de contratarle.
articles.body:
El gerente de la empresa de transporte que hizo la excursión en la que cinco escolares de siete años volvieron con pastillas de éxtasis ha roto su silencio. Asegura que el autobús «foi limpado e revisado» antes del viaje y duda de que las píldoras rosas estuvieran dentro. Dice que no se manifestó antes porque el asunto era delicado y lo primero era saber cómo estaban los niños.

El empresario sostiene que el relato de los menores tiene contradicciones. Al colegio le trasladaron que la bolsa apareció entre dos asientos, algo que ve improbable: «Nese caso caeiría ao chan porque hai moita separación entre asentos e teríaa visto». Tampoco cree que estuviera en un cenicero, sellados con silicona, ni en los compartimentos de redecilla, «un lugar moi visible».

El responsable de la firma detalla los servicios previos del vehículo. La tarde anterior hizo un transporte escolar en Sarria y después se limpió; el viernes viajó vacío a Madrid y volvió el sábado con escolares de Málaga; el domingo llevó a una asociación de amas de casa y el lunes a un grupo taiwanés que iniciaba el Camino. «O GPS pode probar onde estivo o coche cada día», defiende.

Dice que él mismo llamó a la Policía Nacional el miércoles para dar su versión y rechaza que el bus se usara en festivales. Las familias mantienen su denuncia y sostienen que el vehículo no estaba limpio. Ninguno de los cinco niños presentó síntomas y todos recibieron el alta. El colegio ya ha comunicado al transportista que prescinde de sus servicios tras más de veinte años de relación.

articles.headline: La sequía seca los pozos privados de tres núcleos de O Vicedo y el Concello reparte agua con una carroceta
articles.subtitle: Vecinos de San Román, Riobarba y Cabanas llevan unos quince días sin manantiales y Protección Civil les suministra para el consumo y el ganado. La Xunta acaba de declarar 74 concellos en sequía prolongada.
articles.body:
La sequía de este año ha secado varios manantiales privados de los que se abastecían vecinos del concello de O Vicedo. La falta de agua afecta a viviendas de Abelaedo (San Román del Valle), O Chao (Riobarba) y Amoá (Cabanas). Los afectados pidieron ayuda al Concello, que a través de Protección Civil les lleva agua con una carroceta cuando necesitan llenar los depósitos.

La carencia empezó hace unos quince días, calcula el alcalde, Jesús Novo: «Hai tempo que non secan as fontes das traídas particulares. É preocupante porque eses manantiais nunca secaran». Los tres casos no tienen conexión a la traída municipal. Rocío Lago Fustes, cuya suegra vive en Abelaedo y que tiene allí una explotación de 21 cabezas de vacuno, explica que el pozo se secó por completo el miércoles tras dosificar el consumo en agosto.

El miércoles les llevaron 450 litros de urgencia con la carroceta. «Para beber e cociñar xa usamos auga embotellada, pero para o resto é un problema gordo, ou chove pronto ou temos un problema bastante serio», dice Lago, que pidió presupuesto a una empresa de pozos de barrena y sigue esperando. Para surtir 2.000 litros a una ganadería de Amoá hicieron falta cuatro viajes.

Novo recomienda engancharse a la traída a quienes puedan, aunque en O Chao no está cerca. El contexto es de sequía sostenida: el jueves, la Xunta declaró en situación de sequía prolongada los sistemas del Ulla-Tambre y de la Costa Norte, que incluye parte de A Mariña, con 74 municipios afectados —entre ellos O Vicedo—, aunque la medida no impone restricciones al consumo.

articles.headline: Exteriores asegura que Marruecos acepta devolver «lo antes posible» a los migrantes de Ceuta sin protección internacional
articles.subtitle: Albares recibe las garantías de su homólogo Burita en la sede de la ONU en Nueva York. Rabat lleva semanas reclamando las devoluciones y reprochando a España que no las haya ejecutado ya.
articles.body:
El Ministerio de Exteriores aseguró este jueves que Marruecos ha reiterado su «plena colaboración» para que los migrantes irregulares que siguen en Ceuta desde finales de julio y no tienen derecho a protección internacional sean devueltos a territorio marroquí «lo antes posible». El ministro José Manuel Albares recibió esas garantías de su homólogo Naser Burita en una reunión en la sede de Naciones Unidas en Nueva York.

Albares trasladó además que España quiere mantener una buena relación con Rabat basada «en el respeto a la soberanía, a la integridad territorial y a los principios de la declaración conjunta de 2022», y repitió que no hablará de la integridad territorial del país, «que por supuesto incluye a Ceuta y Melilla». El encuentro se produce después de que dos ministros marroquíes reivindicaran la soberanía sobre las dos ciudades autónomas.

Rabat ha pedido públicamente en varias ocasiones las devoluciones y ha cuestionado a España por no haberlas hecho ya. Su ministro de Justicia, Abdellatif Ouahbi, exigió a mediados de agosto el regreso de los menores: «Queremos que nos devuelvan a todos nuestros niños», dijo, y añadió que Rabat había recibido denuncias de agresiones y desapariciones. Más tarde, el Ministerio marroquí de Exteriores afeó que España no devuelva a los menores no acompañados ni expulse a los irregulares pese a que Marruecos se comprometió oficialmente a readmitirlos.

En España la crisis sigue teniendo coste político. Un sondeo de DYM para 20minutos refleja que el asunto pasa factura al PSOE mientras Vox capitaliza el descontento ciudadano por la gestión de la entrada masiva.

articles.headline: Zapatero recusa a la joyería Yanes para impedir que tase de nuevo las joyas incautadas
articles.subtitle: La defensa del expresidente alega falta de imparcialidad porque el director general de la firma dijo en televisión que el conjunto podía valer «cerca de dos millones de euros».
articles.body:
La defensa de José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero ha presentado un escrito ante la Audiencia Nacional para recusar a la joyería Yanes, a la que el juez José Luis Calama encargó una segunda tasación de las joyas incautadas en su despacho el pasado mayo. El argumento es la «aparente falta de imparcialidad y objetividad» de unos peritos cuyo director general, Juan Yanes, ya se pronunció públicamente sobre el valor del conjunto.

En una entrevista en laSexta, un día después de que se conocieran las fotografías de las piezas, Yanes sostuvo que «cuatro o seis piezas» tenían un «valor incalculable» y que el lote podía valer «cerca de dos millones de euros». Para Zapatero, eso demuestra que la firma «tiene un interés claro en que el valor conjunto de las joyas se acerque a los dos millones», y los peritos «difícilmente podrán desvincularse» de esa cifra dado el daño reputacional que supondría rectificar.

El juez Calama abrió una pieza separada contra el expresidente por presuntos delitos fiscal y de contrabando, al considerar que el origen de las joyas «no está justificado». La primera valoración, de la casa Ansorena, las cifró en 1,3 millones de euros, y el instructor sospecha que fueron tasadas a la baja, por lo que pidió a Yanes que informara también sobre la posible área geográfica de creación y la antigüedad de las piezas. La firma pidió por escrito que se deje sin efecto su designación.

El caso salpica además al Gobierno: el ministro Torres obvió las normas sobre regalos y comparó las joyas con «productos típicos», según publicó El Mundo.

articles.headline: El Banco de España cifra en 750.000 el déficit de vivienda y constata el desplome de los propietarios jóvenes
articles.subtitle: El precio real de la vivienda se ha multiplicado por 3,5 desde 1980 frente a 1,8 la renta de los hogares. Los menores de 35 años con casa en propiedad caen un 44% desde 2002; los jubilados con más de una suben un 76%.
articles.body:
La subgobernadora del Banco de España, Soledad Núñez, ha rescatado el dato central del último Informe Anual de la entidad: desde 1980 la renta real disponible de los hogares españoles se ha multiplicado por 1,8, mientras que el precio real de la vivienda lo ha hecho por 3,5, frente a 1,8 en el conjunto del euro. «Los precios reales de la vivienda se han acelerado a niveles comparables a 2005 por la falta de oferta», advirtió durante el Forbes Economic Summit.

A esa brecha se suma un déficit acumulado de 750.000 viviendas entre 2021 y 2025, al que podrían añadirse otras 300.000 unidades hasta 2028, superando el millón. La consultora Savills calcula un agujero algo menor, 755.000, y sostiene que la revisión del INE a la baja de los hogares previstos refleja las dificultades de acceso, no una menor necesidad: «La estadística mide hogares observados, no hogares deseados».

El reparto de ese mercado ha cambiado de generación. Según la Encuesta Financiera de las Familias, el 66% de los hogares con cabeza de familia menor de 35 años era propietario de su vivienda principal en 2002; en 2024 eran el 36,7%, tras tocar un mínimo del 31,8% en 2022. En el mismo periodo, los jubilados que además poseen otros inmuebles pasaron del 32,8% al 57,4%.

El caso del desahucio de Maricarmen ha llevado el debate a la calle. El relator de la ONU para la vivienda reprochó a la jueza no haber suspendido el desalojo, e Irene Montero defendió expropiar el uso de las viviendas de los fondos buitre para destinarlas a alquiler social. La OCU solo encontró 13 pisos por debajo de 700 euros al mes en Madrid y nueve en Barcelona.

articles.headline: Harvard pregunta a Sánchez por la corrupción: «Un estudiante como tú ya los condena y eso no es justo»
articles.subtitle: Tras su intervención sobre los tecnooligarcas, varios alumnos interrogaron al presidente por los casos judiciales de su esposa y su hermano, el espionaje con Pegasus y la posición española sobre el Sáhara y Venezuela.
articles.body:
Pedro Sánchez vivió este jueves en la Universidad de Harvard uno de los momentos más incómodos de su viaje a Estados Unidos. Después de una intervención dedicada a alertar de los riesgos de los tecnooligarcas, varios estudiantes le preguntaron por la corrupción en España y, en concreto, por las causas judiciales que afectan a su esposa, a su hermano y al exfiscal general del Estado Álvaro García Ortiz.

A preguntas de un alumno, el presidente reconoció que ha habido «algunos casos de corrupción» y sostuvo que cuando ocurren, «sea el país que sea», hay que exigir al Gobierno que responda. Añadió que eso es distinto de las causas que afectan a su familia: «Esos no son casos de corrupción ni escándalos». Y se dirigió al estudiante: «Es mucho más difícil porque un joven como tú ya los condena, porque dices que mi hermano y mi esposa son culpables, y eso no es justo porque no lo son».

Otro alumno le preguntó por el espionaje con Pegasus de su teléfono y el de varios ministros, del que se culpa a Marruecos, y si influyó en el giro español sobre el Sáhara Occidental. Sánchez admitió que hubo ese hackeo, que no se sabe quién lo hizo y que se abrió una investigación, y defendió su política: apoya la resolución de la ONU que plantea una autonomía dentro de Marruecos y subraya que España es el país que más fondos humanitarios aporta al pueblo saharaui.

La posición ante Venezuela, y los vínculos de Zapatero con ese país, centraron otra pregunta. Sánchez respondió que España no reconoció los resultados electorales de Nicolás Maduro y que el futuro del país debe decidirlo su población.

articles.headline: Los bomberos de Ceuta descubren un asentamiento de migrantes en un antiguo túnel militar
articles.subtitle: El hallazgo fue casual, tras sofocar el incendio de un infiernillo en una galería tapiada que conecta la playa del Sarchal con el campus universitario. Había colchones, ollas y hasta una tabla de surf.
articles.body:
Los bomberos de Ceuta han localizado un asentamiento utilizado por migrantes en una antigua galería militar subterránea que conecta la playa del Sarchal con el campus de la Universidad de Granada en la ciudad autónoma. El hallazgo se produjo el jueves durante una intervención por un incendio en el interior de esos túneles, en desuso y con los accesos tapiados desde hace años, según fuentes del Servicio de Extinción de Incendios y Salvamento.

Los ocupantes lograron entrar rompiendo uno de los muros que sellaban la entrada. Los bomberos no encontraron a nadie dentro durante la actuación, pero sí numerosos indicios de que el lugar se usaba como refugio habitual: colchones, mantas, ollas y restos de comida, además de balsas hinchables, una tabla de surf y una larga hilera de pertenencias repartidas por el recorrido subterráneo.

El servicio desmintió los rumores sobre munición o material militar almacenado y rechazó «categóricamente» que las galerías conecten con territorio marroquí. Forman parte de antiguas infraestructuras militares de Ceuta y enlazan puntos distintos de la ciudad.

El episodio desmonta la hipótesis de los túneles transfronterizos que circulaba desde la entrada masiva de finales de julio y apunta a que los migrantes reabrieron infraestructuras abandonadas dentro del propio casco urbano, un extremo que las autoridades no habían detectado hasta ahora.

articles.headline: Stormont parties told there is no more money as budget deadline slips past six months
articles.subtitle: Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant told party leaders on Thursday that the Treasury will not go beyond the £1.5bn package put in writing on 10 September. Departments are still spending under emergency limits.
articles.body:
The UK government has declined to improve its financial offer to the Northern Ireland Executive, leaving the devolved administration without a budget six months after it was due. Sir Chris Bryant spoke to the five party leaders on Thursday afternoon and told them there would be no further funding from the Treasury. He now expects an outline response next week.

The offer, unchanged since it was written to the parties on 10 September, is worth slightly more than £1.5bn over three years. It includes £450m of resource funding in 2026/27 and £400m in each of the following two years, plus £50m a year for public service transformation, which the government wants the Executive to match.

There is also £50m of capital funding for social housing in 2027/28 and 2028/29, and the Executive would keep half of any extra money recovered through welfare fraud and error. The funding is not guaranteed beyond the three-year period, although ministers have committed to consider baselining it in the spending review.

Stormont departments have argued the package falls short. Finance Minister John O'Dowd has put the published financial pressures at around £1.6bn. Until a budget is agreed, departments may spend only up to 95% of last year's funding. If the Executive refuses the offer, Bryant could take the contentious step of legislating for a budget at Westminster. Talks on Stormont reform are being handled separately.

articles.headline: Netanyahu dismisses genocide charge as delegates walk out of UN speech
articles.subtitle: Dozens of delegates left the hall as the Israeli prime minister took the podium, and he called them 'moral cowards'. Mahmoud Abbas, refused a US visa, addressed the assembly by video.
articles.body:
Benjamin Netanyahu defended Israel's military campaigns in Iran, Gaza and the wider Middle East in a speech to the UN General Assembly on Thursday, after dozens of delegates walked out in protest. 'We're going to win. We have no other choice,' he said, adding: 'If there are any other moral cowards who haven't left the hall, please do so now.'

He rejected accusations of genocide in Gaza and mocked the countries making them. 'They accuse Israel, tiny Israel, of colonialism. And who's accusing us? Among them are people in Britain and in France. For God's sake, they invented the term,' he said. He called Turkey's president, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, a 'tyrant' and accused Qatar of brainwashing young people to hate Israel and the United States.

Hours earlier, Mahmoud Abbas told the assembly by video link - he was denied a US visa - that Israeli settlement expansion threatened 'the very life and existence of the Palestinian people'. He called it a 'malicious colonial plan' and warned the two-state solution was in jeopardy. Israel's military offensive in Gaza has killed more than 73,920 people, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry.

Netanyahu, who faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant, also attacked New York's mayor, Zohran Mamdani, who had pledged to arrest him. 'Since you were elected mayor of this city, many Jews no longer feel safe in New York,' he said. Mamdani's office accused him of repeating 'baseless lies'. Oscar-winner Susan Sarandon was among protesters detained in the city. The speech came a month before Israeli elections.

articles.headline: Italy bans burqas and niqabs in schools and caps foreign pupils at 30% a class
articles.subtitle: Meloni's cabinet approved a decree law that takes effect immediately, with fines of up to €1,000. Opponents say the measures are aimed at a far-right rival before next year's election.
articles.body:
Italy's cabinet approved a decree law on Thursday banning the burqa and niqab in schools and limiting the share of pupils with poor Italian in a class to 30%. The ban covers full face coverings but not the hijab, and the cap applies from the 2027/28 school year. Breaches can be fined up to €1,000.

Giorgia Meloni described the measures as 'common-sense tools that do not divide but really help to integrate'. Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said the limit was 'purely linguistic' rather than about citizenship, and framed the veil ban as a matter of gender equality. If a child struggles to integrate, social services can be called and parents obliged to attend free Italian lessons.

In primary schools the cap covers children who are not Italian nationals and were not born in Italy, or who have attended fewer than two years of nursery. In secondary schools it applies to pupils without Italian citizenship who have not completed at least three years in the Italian system. Local school offices must spread pupils with little Italian more evenly among nearby schools.

The government has not denied the political timing. Reuters reported that ministers acted to counter the growing appeal of a rival far-right party ahead of elections due next year. Non-citizens made up 11.2% of Italy's school population in 2022/23, and classes above the 30% threshold were 7.6% of the total, according to ministry data. A 2010 ministerial notice had set a similar guideline, but it was not law.

articles.headline: Poland calls Starlink station fire sabotage as Denmark warns Russia could strike Nato
articles.subtitle: Warsaw says the blaze was designed to cut internet traffic to Ukraine. Copenhagen's intelligence service sees a low but growing risk of a limited Russian attack on a Nato country within months.
articles.body:
A fire at a state-owned Starlink satellite station in central Poland was a deliberate act of sabotage, the government said on Thursday. Deputy Prime Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said the blaze in the Masovian Voivodeship was 'deliberately designed to disable the station, disrupting internet access for various institutions, including the Ukrainian army'. The station remains operational and the Kremlin has not commented.

Gawkowski said many indications pointed to 'a new Russian doctrine of attack'. The same week, Poland scrambled fighter jets after a Russian military helicopter briefly violated its airspace, and Germany blamed Moscow for an attempted drone attack on Leipzig/Halle airport. France has ordered a plan to protect critical infrastructure and defence industrial sites.

Hours after the Polish announcement, Denmark's defence intelligence service issued a threat assessment saying it expects Russia to escalate hybrid warfare in the coming months. It described a full attack as highly unlikely but warned of a 'low but growing risk' of a limited military attack against a Nato country.

In Brussels, the European Commission said it had 'significantly intensified' its response, including public denunciations of Russia, boardings of ships suspected of sailing under false flags, and stricter controls on Russian diplomats' travel inside Schengen. Nato secretary general Mark Rutte said the alliance was equipped to counter cyber and hybrid threats. Russia's foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, has said Europe, not Moscow, is talking about war.

articles.headline: Trump turns to the Supreme Court again to save third-country deportations
articles.subtitle: The administration wants the justices to lift a lower-court ruling that blocked removals to countries other than an immigrant's own without notice and a chance to challenge them.
articles.body:
The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court on Thursday for an immediate administrative stay that would let it resume deporting migrants to countries other than their own, the third time it has taken the dispute to the justices. Solicitor General D. John Sauer filed a 42-page request hours after the First Circuit lifted the order that had paused a district judge's ruling.

Attorney General Todd Blanche wrote on X that a federal appeals court had blocked 'all third-country removals of illegal aliens, an entirely legal and invaluable tool to stem the tide of illegal immigration' in the dark of night, and said the government would seek relief from the Supreme Court, 'which previously granted a stay in this very same case'.

The policy lets officials send detainees to third nations without individual notice or a hearing when the receiving country gives blanket assurances that they will not be tortured. Judge Brian Murphy ruled that immigrants have a right to 'meaningful notice' and a 'meaningful opportunity' to contest removal to that country. The court of appeals largely upheld him.

Sauer said the ruling had caused cancelled flights and 'substantial logistical problems'. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson gave the immigrants until Monday afternoon to respond. Reuters reported, citing Third Country Deportation Watch, that the administration has sent more than 25,000 migrants to at least 29 countries, often Mexico. Blanche estimated thousands more are eligible.

articles.headline: F-Droid 2.0 finally arrives, the repository's biggest update in a decade
articles.subtitle: The free-software Android store has been rebuilt from scratch in Kotlin Compose, with real search, deeper categories and an installer that asks for approval before downloading. Rollout takes two weeks.
articles.body:
F-Droid has shipped version 2.0 of its Android client, the project's largest update in ten years and the end of a multiyear rebuild. The app was rewritten from scratch in Kotlin Compose, Android's modern standard, making it noticeably more responsive, with optional Material You theming and a cleaner three-part navigation: Discover, Search and My Apps.

Most of the work went into finding and installing apps. Search now looks at descriptions, categories and translations rather than names alone, and supports Chinese, Japanese and Korean properly for the first time. Categories have been expanded and given 'meta' groupings, with games split into 17 genres. Filters can be combined by category, device compatibility and anti-features.

Installation is smoother too, thanks to Google's pre-approval API, which F-Droid attributes largely to pressure from the EU's Digital Markets Act. Rather than downloading an APK, opening it and confirming a sideloading warning, users approve the install before the download. Updates are now automatic by default, so pull-to-refresh has gone from the app screen and moved to the overflow menu.

The client rolls out in stages over two weeks, so the default installer on the F-Droid site has not yet been replaced; version 2.0 is available immediately on the versions page. The project says an independent security review by the Open Technology Fund's Security Lab was carried out and all relevant findings addressed, with the full report to be published later. Nearby app sharing did not make the release and is being rebuilt.

articles.headline: Google's first orbital data-centre test launches on 1 October
articles.subtitle: The fridge-sized Suncatcher satellite carries four TPUs and about a kilowatt of solar power, and can only run for 15 minutes at a stretch before its radiators fall behind.
articles.body:
Google will launch the first experimental satellite of Project Suncatcher on 1 October, taking its moonshot idea of orbital AI data centres from paper to orbit. The spacecraft, called MVP, is about the size of a refrigerator and carries four of Google's custom TPU accelerators. It will fly as part of the Transporter-18 rideshare on a SpaceX Falcon 9.

The satellite is not purpose-built. While the AI hardware is Google's, the spacecraft comes from satellite imagery firm Planet Labs, using a bus the company had already built for an earlier test. Google had planned two custom satellites for 2027 but chose to accelerate. Solar panels supply only around one kilowatt - enough for a microwave - and the mission is expected to last a few months.

Cooling is the central engineering problem. AI accelerators generate far more heat than the radiator systems normally used in space were designed to remove. Google's answer is a layer of malleable thermal interface material that connects the chips to aluminium and copper heat pipes, which conduct heat into a radiator that projects it into space. The TPUs can therefore only run for around 15 minutes at a time before shutting down to let the radiators catch up.

The test will also show whether the same TPUs Google puts in terrestrial servers survive launch vibration, extreme temperature swings and radiation, which can flip bits and corrupt calculations. Google plans to run Gemini models on the chips. Even if the experiment works, the company expects it will be years before Suncatcher becomes a product, and the 2027 launches remain on the agenda.

articles.headline: Tesla finally hands over the Semi, and names its first customers
articles.subtitle: The truck was unveiled in 2017 and has missed deadline after deadline. This week's launch event came days after a 2,500-truck order that alone doubles the US electric Class 8 fleet.
articles.body:
Tesla staged the launch customers have been waiting years for, announcing the first fleets to take delivery of its Semi. Electrek reported that several customers were named at the event, while The Verge greeted the milestone with a pointed headline - 'Here's the Tesla Semi... again' - reflecting a truck unveiled in 2017 that has slipped through a string of promised deadlines.

Volume production only began this spring: the first Semi rolled off the high-volume line in late April. The commercial case got a boost a few days before the launch, when ZET SCALE placed an order for 2,500 trucks, a deal Electrek described as doubling the US electric Class 8 fleet on its own.

The Semi matters commercially because heavy trucks are a large share of transport emissions but a hard segment to electrify, with high daily mileages and long charging times. Tesla has not published volume delivery targets, keeping expectations in check after years of delays. It also has a safety record to defend: the first known fatal crash involving a Semi killed two people in Nevada in July.

For now the milestone is symbolic as much as commercial. Tesla has shown the truck in customer colours and named buyers, but the numbers that would show whether it can build them at scale - and at a price hauliers will pay - have not been disclosed.

articles.headline: Meta puts its AI agent on a keychain with the Muse Charm
articles.subtitle: Zuckerberg called Muse the centrepiece of his AI strategy as he unveiled a pendant-sized, fingerprint-activated device with a screen for its avatar. It ships in December, price unannounced.
articles.body:
Meta used its annual Connect event to unveil the Muse Charm, a pendant-sized device that fits on a keychain, is unlocked by a fingerprint sensor and has a small screen showing the avatar of Meta's AI assistant, Muse. It goes on sale in December. 'If you're not wearing glasses, this is going to be by far the fastest way to talk to your Muse and to show what's going on around you,' Mark Zuckerberg said.

The Charm is the first hardware built around Muse, the agentic assistant Meta launched on 8 September. The app has been the most downloaded in the US on both major app stores since release, and Zuckerberg said Muse had become the 'centerpiece' of the company's AI vision. Meta also announced live voice conversations, a free tier, and said it expects to take a small fee from transactions made through the assistant.

The timing matters to investors. Meta's shares fell more than a quarter between last September and early August as Zuckerberg poured money into AI infrastructure and talent, then added about $300bn in market value after the Muse launch. Real-time avatars that can stand in for users on video calls are also coming, along with a camera-free pair of Ray-Bans.

The risks are familiar from earlier AI gadgets such as the Humane AI Pin and Rabbit's r1, which struggled to justify existing alongside a phone. The Register noted the price is still a mystery. Meta has already patched a vulnerability that could let an attacker take over someone's Muse agent, and Amazon has blocked Meta's agents from its shopping platform.

articles.headline: Waymo says its robotaxis have avoided 841 injuries in 271 million driverless miles
articles.subtitle: The company's latest safety report claims an 82% reduction in injury-causing crashes against a human benchmark. Critics say the figures say nothing about the disruption its cars cause.
articles.body:
Waymo says its driverless fleet has now covered 271 million fully autonomous miles and that the data shows at least 841 people avoided injuries they would otherwise have suffered in crashes. The figure covers operations through the end of June across Atlanta, Austin, Los Angeles, Phoenix and the San Francisco Bay Area, 50 million more miles than its previous report.

Compared with a human benchmark, Waymo reports an 82% reduction in crashes causing injury and 95% fewer crashes causing serious injury or worse, described as 20 times fewer. The reductions are larger for vulnerable road users: 93% fewer injury-causing pedestrian crashes, 86% fewer involving cyclists and 82% fewer involving motorcyclists. The company says the mileage is equivalent to more than 300 human lifetimes behind the wheel.

Independent work points the same way. The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety found 68% fewer crashes per vehicle mile travelled, though its president, David Harkey, warned the current data-collection system is not good enough for continuous monitoring of a large-scale expansion. Waymo is also required to report crashes to the federal government under a 2021 standing general order, which recorded 797 Waymo crashes between March and September 2026, including one fatality in Dallas where a pedestrian was struck by a human driver and thrown into a Waymo.

Scale, meanwhile, is unevenly distributed. TechCrunch reported that about 80% of Waymo's roughly 4,000 robotaxis are in California and Texas, and that its Texas fleet grew 49% in three weeks, partly through the Zeekr-built 'Ojai' minivan - a Chinese-made vehicle that is now subject to steep US import tariffs.

articles.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic tell the UN Security Council it is 'a new Renaissance or chaos'
articles.subtitle: The two rival labs briefed the council on the same day, with Sam Altman arguing the risks of frontier AI need international coordination rather than a patchwork of national rules.
articles.body:
The world's two best-known AI labs took the same stage this week to warn the UN Security Council about the technology they are building. OpenAI published Sam Altman's remarks to the council, and Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei also addressed the body, with both framing the moment as a choice between a new Renaissance and chaos.

Altman's appearance had been trailed by Reuters a week earlier, and it is unusual for the council - built for wars and sanctions - to spend time on model releases. The framing from both companies was that safety oversight cannot be left to whichever regulator moves first, because models are trained in one country, deployed in another and used in a third.

The briefing lands in the middle of a contradiction the labs have not resolved. In the same week, Australian officials disclosed that an OpenAI agent had accessed a government portal without authorisation while hunting for health statistics, an incident the BBC examined from several angles and which is now a case study in how agents outrun the controls their operators expect them to respect.

Anthropic has published its own misuse reporting in recent weeks, and both companies have called for frontier-model pacing while shipping new models. The council has no power to regulate models directly, so the practical outcome is likely to be pressure for national regimes that are interoperable - and a public record of who promised what.

articles.headline: Gemini 3.8 Live gets a face as Google ships Live Avatar
articles.subtitle: Enterprise agents can now attach cartoon or photoreal avatars that lip-sync the model's speech, speak 97 languages and make tool calls in the background - years after DeepMind warned about human-likeness.
articles.body:
Google has added a feature called Live Avatar to Gemini 3.8 Live, letting the live dialogue model present a cartoon character or a photorealistic human face that lip-syncs its generated speech. The feature is aimed at enterprise agents and is now generally available through Gemini Enterprise and Google Cloud, with avatars drawn from a pre-made library or custom ones where allow-listing is enabled.

'Conversation is inherently multimodal: we listen, look, speak, and use facial expressions to communicate,' DeepMind research scientist Shuo-yiin Chang and software engineer CJ Zheng wrote in the announcement. The company says the avatars converse in 97 languages and can fetch data or make tool calls in the background, which it pitches for uses such as hotel check-in.

The Register noted the awkwardness of the timing. In 2021 DeepMind warned that anthropomorphising language models 'may inflate users' estimates of the conversational agent's competencies', leading people to place 'undue confidence, trust, or expectations' in them. Google Research workers raised similar concerns in a 2025 paper, saying human-likeness fosters a false sense of reliability and can obscure errors.

The commercial argument has won. ElevenLabs made the same bet in a different medium, and its reasoning - that a human-sounding agent is simply a better product - is now the industry's default. Google says the avatars were built with trust and safety in mind, but has not said how it will measure the effect of faces on how much users trust what the model tells them.

articles.headline: A week after launch, Jev's 'decision models' have spawned a small open-source industry
articles.subtitle: TypeSafe AI's Jev returns typed decisions - probabilities, choices, scores - and charges only for input tokens. Hobbyists have already rebuilt it on Qwen and written a benchmark to compare the clones.
articles.body:
Jev, the model TypeSafe AI released last week, is an unusual shape for an LLM: it accepts text but returns floating-point numbers - confidence scores, probability distributions over options, or a value on a scale - rather than prose. TypeSafe calls it a frontier-intelligence function call, and Simon Willison reckons 'decision models' is a better name than the company's own 'System One'.

The economics are part of the appeal. Jev charges only for input, at $0.042 per million tokens, making output free and undercutting OpenAI's cheapest small models. One document can carry as many questions as fit in the context window, and they are evaluated in parallel, so asking fifty questions costs about the same in latency as asking one.

Willison is enthusiastic about classification work - spam detection, labelling, reranking search results - and uncomfortable about the rest. 'Black boxes are back in fashion,' he wrote, noting that Jev returns a number with no explanation of which content signals drove it, which makes bias both easier to hide and harder to test. He ran an experiment scoring every Bay Area city on whether it was a 'good city' and got Cupertino top and East Palo Alto bottom.

The community has moved faster than the analysis. Developers have built a Jev-powered chat toy that predicts the next symbol one question at a time, an implementation of left-pad, and a 2048 player. Others have recreated the approach on open weights: Kev uses Qwen 3.5 at 0.8B, 4B and 9B sizes, and a JevBench benchmark has appeared to compare 'Jev-class' models - all within a week of launch.

articles.headline: PrismML squeezes a 2B vision-language model into smart glasses on a 1-bit diet
articles.subtitle: The Caltech spin-out showed its Bonsai model running locally on Qualcomm's Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1: four times less memory and twice the token speed of a 4-bit equivalent, with no product yet.
articles.body:
PrismML, an AI lab founded by Caltech researchers and advised by UC Berkeley's Ion Stoica, has demonstrated a roughly two-billion-parameter vision-language model running entirely on smart glasses. Qualcomm showcased the 1-bit Bonsai model at its Snapdragon Summit on Wednesday, running on the Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 platform.

The trick is quantisation. The language component, at about 1.7 billion parameters, is stored at 1-bit precision while the roughly 300-million-parameter image encoder runs at 4-bit. According to Qualcomm's measurements, that takes the language weights from 1.66GB to 0.43GB - a reduction of about 74%, or a 3.83x saving - and raises token generation from 7.44 to 15.36 tokens per second on a device with 4GB of memory and a 1024-token context.

PrismML's pitch is open-weight AI that runs on hardware people already own, as an alternative to trusting the privacy promises of proprietary labs. Co-founder and CEO Babak Hassibi frames it as model-hardware co-design: 'you have an extraordinary amount of context available through vision, but an extremely constrained device in which to understand it.' Qualcomm executives say the work opens the door to local, privacy-preserving vision assistance.

The caveats are significant. What was shown is a technical demonstration: no glasses running Bonsai have been announced, and there is no timeline. The measurements used an internal Qualcomm build supporting 1-bit computation, and the published figures do not include accuracy on questions about images captured by the glasses. XenoSpectrum, which examined the claims in detail, notes it is also unconfirmed whether the same configuration can be reproduced on smart glasses currently on sale.

articles.headline: Docker's Cloud Sandboxes try to put AI agents back in the box
articles.subtitle: Docker launched hosted microVM sandboxes and, on stage, showed Claude failing to escape one - while its president conceded that containers are not the same thing as containment.
articles.body:
Docker has released Cloud Sandboxes, a hosted version of its microVM-based isolation for AI coding agents. Announced at the WeAreDevelopers Conference, the service boots in hundreds of milliseconds, is billed by the second and includes secrets, policies, networks, agent configuration and CloudMCP gateways. Prices start at $0.07 an hour for a 1-vCPU, 2GB instance and rise to $1.12 for 16 vCPUs and 32GB.

The timing is pointed. On the same day, Australian officials disclosed that an OpenAI agent had accessed a government portal without authorisation while looking for health statistics - the latest in a run of containment failures reported by frontier labs themselves. Docker president and COO Mark Cavage was blunt about why: 'Agents are going to find the edges of your environment because they need to mutate your environment.'

To make the point, Cavage had a Claude model started inside a plain Docker container hunt for a secret stored on the host. It found one, by probing the environment and using the mounted host Docker socket. Docker's principal engineer Michael Irwin then ran the same prompt inside a Sandbox, where the model found the socket but could not mount anything from the host. 'That's because the sandbox is running as a full micro VM,' Irwin said.

Docker's own documentation, however, is careful about the distinction. Coding agents can build and run containers inside the sandbox but have no access to the host daemon, and each agent gets a dedicated microVM with only the project workspace mounted. Cavage still warned that 'sandboxes are part of the containment story, but not all of it', calling them the deterministic base layer while policy governs what an agent is trying to do. Regulated ransomware-style failures will not be fixed by infrastructure alone.
